fields.v: De La Cruz, E. (2026). From Code-Centric to Intent-Centric Software Engineering: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Generative AI, Agentic Systems, and Engineering Accountability. arXiv:2605.11027v1 [cs.SE], 10 May 2026
Preprint — arXiv; manuscript prepared for journal submission (competing-interest statement 'should be updated before submission'); no venue stated
Academia: University of the Cumberlands, United States (single author)

Conceptual — qualitative public-discourse and document analysis (reflexive thematic analysis, IPA-informed) of peer-reviewed literature, preprints/benchmarks and public thought-leadership artefacts (talks, interviews, X posts); produces themes, a dichotomy matrix, a maturity pathway and a research agenda. Not a review: no search sources or procedure described
fields.why: Judgement: qualitative public-discourse/document analysis with inclusion/exclusion criteria (p. 3-4) but no sources searched, search procedure, dates or corpus size, so not a review under the 2026-11-23 rule. Another reader could file it as an empirical qualitative study; that would change Q13 (N/A) but Q3-Q8 would still score little, as no agent, model or task is involved

fields.v: N/A: no SDD approach or tool studied; general 'intent-centric software engineering' paradigm ('prompt as specification' appears only as a code)

None prescribed. Recommends machine-readable context for agents: decision records, dependency maps, interface contracts, threat models, non-functional requirements; 'requirements and architecture decisions become machine-readable context' (Stage 4)
N/A (no workflow; generic agent loop 'plan, retrieve context, edit files, run commands, observe test results, repair errors, prepare a pull request' described in Theme 2)
Not specified as a flow. Argues for review gates, approval workflows and humans as 'accountable operators' deciding acceptance of generated artefacts
N/A. Corpus size not stated; theme support counts 7-25 artefacts per theme (Table 5)
N/A (no participants; public figures such as Karpathy, Ng, Ozkaya, Willison, Dohmke, Cherny analysed as cases)
None (qualitative themes; source-support counts per theme, explicitly 'not statistical weight')

Manual qualitative coding by the single author: semantic and latent coding, idiographic case memos, recursive theme development, triangulation with peer-reviewed literature, 'structured adversarial audit'; no inter-rater reliability by design

N/A. Findings: eight themes (natural language as programming interface; agentic workflow over single prompt; humans as architects/verifiers/accountable operators; democratisation vs professionalisation; reasoning/autonomy contested; safety/governance/provenance debt; convergence with AI systems engineering; essential complexity and technical debt persist); core dichotomy acceleration vs accountability; 5-stage maturity pathway

Not a participant interview study; themes are propositions to be tested. Public discourse is performative/strategic, over-represents prominent voices and under-represents ordinary engineers; X/YouTube sources unstable; maturity pathway is a projection, not a prediction; rapid tool change; tool heterogeneity; mixed productivity evidence. Research agenda: long-term technical debt of AI code, review practices, repository structures for safe agentic development, junior learning, governance models, benchmarks covering architecture/security/maintainability

Corpus size, search procedure and dates of collection not reported. Supplemental package (corpus register, codebook, coding matrix, etc.) 'prepared for' Zenodo/GitHub release, no DOI or URL given. Generative AI used for consistency and writing support. No pre-registration. Not specific to SDD; mentions agentic tools (Claude Code, Copilot coding agent, Codex) only as public product artefacts. Programming language: N/A
Partly (0.5): workflow, inclusion/exclusion criteria and coding framework described; corpus size, search procedure and the corpus itself not available
Partly (0.5): themes framed as propositions, but abstract states 'the analysis shows' and claims such as bounded autonomy preserving quality are not supported by evidence in the paper
fields.why: Judgement: themes are framed as 'transparent qualitative propositions' (p. 13, 19) and limitations stated (could be Yes), but the abstract says 'the analysis shows' and that bounded autonomy 'can preserve quality, security, maintainability, and trust' (p. 1), which the paper does not show (Partly)
